items.title: Giga Storage Secures €450M for Belgian BESS Giant
items.summary: Giga Storage closed a €450 million (US$512 million) financing package for its Green Turtle battery storage project in Belgium, which will have 700MW of power capacity and 2,800MWh of energy storage. Construction is set to begin in September following the financial close in early July.

items.title: Tesla Deploys Record 13.5 GWh of Storage in Q2
items.summary: Tesla announced it deployed 13.5 GWh of energy storage capacity globally in the second quarter of 2026, a 53% jump from Q1 and 40% higher than the same period last year. The company's total deployments since 2016 now exceed 132 GWh, and investors are watching for further detail at its July 22 earnings call.

items.title: BYD and Greenvolt Plan 2.4GWh Polish BESS Project
items.summary: BYD Energy Storage and Greenvolt Power will co-develop a 600 MW/2.4 GWh battery storage facility in Siedlce, Poland, with construction targeted to start in Q3 2026 and operation by the end of 2027. The project is one of several gigawatt-scale European deployments announced alongside Envision Energy's 400 MW/1,600 MWh system in northern Germany.

items.title: German BESS Deal-Making Accelerates Among Majors
items.summary: TotalEnergies and Kyon, Envision Energy and Ju:niz, and Flower have all announced significant German battery storage project developments and acquisitions this week, reflecting intensifying competition in the market. Separately, Chint Solar Europe signed a portfolio deal for seven ready-to-build BESS projects in Germany with Flower Infrastructure Technologies.

items.title: US Storage Costs Rise, Reversing Prior-Year Declines
items.summary: Lazard's annual benchmarking report found that the levelised cost of storage (LCOS) for utility-scale battery systems in the US has risen this year, reversing the declines reported in the 2025 edition. The increase comes amid ongoing tariff and supply chain pressures affecting US developers.

items.title: Unigrid Launches 25-Year Sodium-Ion Home Battery
items.summary: Unigrid has launched its NaCasa sodium-ion home battery system in Europe, rated for a 25-year lifespan, with a US rollout planned for a later date. The launch is part of a broader wave of sodium-ion commercialization moves this month from Peak Energy and ESS Tech as well.

items.title: Peak Energy, ESS Tech, Unigrid Push Sodium-Ion Forward
items.summary: Peak Energy, ESS Tech Inc, and Unigrid have made recent announcements advancing sodium-ion energy storage technology in the US and Europe. The moves reflect accelerating momentum behind sodium-ion as a lower-cost alternative to lithium-ion for stationary storage applications.

items.title: Chinese Sodium Cells Match Key Tesla Performance Benchmarks
items.summary: A new independent teardown study of a commercial Hina sodium-ion battery found its performance surprisingly close to established lithium-ion benchmarks, based on impedance spectroscopy testing of 120 cells. Researchers evaluated the cells across current levels and temperatures ranging from -20°C to 45°C to assess real-world viability for grid and EV use.

items.title: Peak Energy to Build 4GWh Sodium-Ion Factory in California
items.summary: Sodium-ion startup Peak Energy is building a $71 million factory intended to be the first US facility dedicated to grid-scale sodium-ion energy storage systems, with shipments expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027. The plant underscores a broader industry shift toward domestic sodium-ion manufacturing capacity.

items.title: CATL Clears Technical Hurdles for Sodium-Ion Mass Production
items.summary: CATL said it has overcome four key barriers this year, including extreme water control, gas generation in hard carbon, aluminum foil adhesion, and self-forming anode systems, paving the way for full-scale sodium-ion mass production by the end of 2026. Its sodium-ion packs reportedly retain 90% usable capacity even at -40°C, aiding cold-climate grid and EV applications.

items.title: Australia Adds 11 Projects to Renewable Priority List
items.summary: Australia's federal government has added 11 new generation and energy storage projects to its National Renewable Energy Priority List, expanding the pipeline of assets eligible for expedited support. The move comes alongside separate news that CSIRO revised pumped hydro storage costs upward in its annual GenCost report.

items.title: Leaked EU Plan Calls for 200GW of Storage by 2030
items.summary: According to a leaked draft of its Electrification Action Plan, the European Union must deploy 200GW of energy storage by 2030 to meet energy system flexibility needs. The draft signals an aggressive future policy push tied to the bloc's broader electrification and decarbonization goals.

items.title: Thailand Sets New Market Rules to Spur Storage Investment
items.summary: New market rules will encourage investment in energy storage as a key component of Thailand's national energy vision, according to the country's energy ministry. The rules are intended to accelerate deployment in support of the country's broader clean-energy transition strategy.

items.title: Queensland Shelves AU$6 Billion Pumped Hydro Project
items.summary: The Queensland government has reportedly shelved the proposed AU$6 billion (US$4 billion) Mt Rawdon pumped hydro project, ending state support for a mine-repurposing scheme that had attracted AU$50 million in government funding. The decision marks a policy setback for long-duration storage development in the state.

items.title: FERC Presses Grid Operators on Large-Load Integration Rules
items.summary: FERC issued tailored show-cause orders under Section 206 of the Federal Power Act to all six regional grid operators, directing them to justify or reform rules governing how data centers and other large loads, including those co-located with battery storage, connect to the grid. The action builds on a December 2025 order directing PJM to adopt transparent co-location tariff rules and follows a Department of Energy directive to expedite large-load integration.
